units.text: INT. FIELD HOSPITAL TENT - NIGHT
Canvas walls breathing in the wind.
A generator rattles outside.
Kerosene lamps cast long shadows over a row of cots, most empty.
DR. SOLEDAD ARRIAGA (40s, sleeves rolled to the elbow, hair clipped under a cap) leans over a cot where a young soldier lies unconscious, his chest rising in shallow, uneven breaths.
Her hands move with the economy of long practice: a pulse at the wrist, a lifted eyelid, a pressed palm on the sternum.
Opposite her, a nurse, SISTER AGNES KOWALSKI (50s, wimple, a rosary peeking from her apron pocket), wrings out a cloth in a basin and lays it on the boy's forehead.
How long since the last dose?
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: Forty minutes.
units.name: AGNES

units.text: And his pressure?
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: Falling.
units.name: AGNES

units.text: Soledad takes a breath.
Straightens.
Her gaze drifts to the tent flap, where the wind has begun to tug at the canvas ties.
Prepare the table. We're opening him.
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: Doctor, without plasma...
units.name: AGNES

units.text: Then without plasma.
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: Agnes hesitates, her fingers at the rosary.
Then she moves, quick and quiet, to the instrument tray.
The tent flap tears open.
A gust of cold air swirls through the tent, snuffing two of the lamps.
In the doorway stands a tall, soaked figure, rain streaming from the brim of his helmet.
COLONEL AUGUSTIN RENARD (50s, medals dulled by mud, one arm in a sling) takes a step inside.
Behind him, nothing but darkness and the sound of far-off guns.
Doctor Arriaga.
units.name: RENARD

units.text: Colonel. This is not a good moment.
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: It is the only moment I have.
units.name: RENARD

units.text: He glances at the boy on the cot.
His jaw tightens.
That one is mine.
units.name: RENARD

units.text: Then you may watch.
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: Agnes holds out the scalpel.
Soledad takes it.
Renard removes his helmet and stands very still while the generator coughs and the lamps flicker, and the first incision is made.
